_comment: Environment variables that scripts/check-env-coverage.mjs finds in the code
but that must NOT appear in .env.example, each with the reason it is exempt.
An entry whose read site disappears is reported as stale and fails the screen,
so this file cannot accumulate exemptions for code that has since gone.

entries.name: NEXT_PHASE
entries.reason: Set by Next.js itself, never by an operator. instrumentation.ts:61 reads it to skip database work during a build phase. Documenting it would invite someone to set it.

entries.name: NEXT_RUNTIME
entries.reason: Set by Next.js per runtime entry (nodejs/edge). instrumentation.ts:9,101 dispatch on it. An operator setting it would desynchronise the code from the bundle it is loaded into.

entries.name: VITEST
entries.reason: Set by the Vitest runner when it loads the test files. lib/errors-server.ts:216 uses it to relax error handling in tests only. Never part of a deployment's configuration.

entries.name: CI
entries.reason: Set by the GitHub Actions runner. scripts/migrate.ts:169 reads it to refuse an interactive prompt with no terminal. Not a NuCRM knob.

entries.name: USER
entries.reason: Not read: lib/db/pool.ts:164 contains the string 'process.env.USER' inside a warning message explaining that the pg client falls back to the OS user. Matched by this screen's extractor; exempted rather than reworded so the warning keeps its exact wording.

entries.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_DATABASE_URL
entries.reason: MUST NEVER BE SET. lib/keepalive.ts is unreachable dead code, and because it reads a NEXT_PUBLIC_ name, adopting it would inline a live Postgres connection string — credentials and all — into the JavaScript shipped to every browser. The hazard is recorded in the readiness report instead of being documented here as if it were a normal option.

entries.name: BASE_URL
entries.reason: Generic CLI-style parameter for scripts/lighthouse-audit.ts (defaults to http://localhost:3000). Passing BASE_URL in a shared shell environment would also be picked up by unrelated tooling, which is why it is a one-shot prefix rather than a .env entry.

entries.name: OUTPUT
entries.reason: Format selector for scripts/lighthouse-audit.ts (json/html/both). Far too generic a name to reserve in a deployment env file; set per invocation.

entries.name: SKIP_LIGHTHOUSE
entries.reason: Escape hatch for scripts/quality-report.ts to skip the browser run when no Chrome is available (CI). A report-behaviour flag, not application configuration.

entries.name: CI_MIN_SCORE
entries.reason: Pass mark for scripts/quality-report.ts (default 80). Tuned in the workflow that calls it, so a workflow edit and a config edit cannot disagree about the threshold.

entries.name: E2E_BASE_URL
entries.reason: Target origin for scripts/preprod-api-e2e.ts (default http://127.0.0.1:3100). Chosen by whatever is running the suite against an environment; not something an operator configures on a deploy.

entries.name: STRESS_BATCH
entries.reason: Row count per batch for scripts/stress-test.ts (default 100). Load-generation tuning for the person running the test.

entries.name: STRICT
entries.reason: Makes scripts/preflight.ts treat warnings as failures. A mode flag for the caller, and a name generic enough that reserving it in .env.example would collide with other tools.

entries.name: COMPOSE_FILE
entries.reason: Docker Compose's own variable, interpreted by the compose binary before any NuCRM process starts. scripts/check-running-config-drift.mjs:194 reads it only to work out which files compose is using. Belongs to compose, not to this app.

entries.name: COMPOSE_FILES
entries.reason: NuCRM's multi-file variant of the above, set by the deploy tooling that invokes compose. Paths to files already in the repository; nothing for an operator to choose per deployment.

entries.name: COMPOSE_PROJECT
entries.reason: Compose project name used by scripts/check-running-config-drift.mjs:59 to find the running containers. Default 'deploy' is what the repository's own compose setup uses.

entries.name: ACCEPTANCE_BASE_URL
entries.reason: Read only by scripts/simulate-basecrm-acceptance.ts to point the live acceptance harness at a dev server (defaults to http://localhost:3100). It is a local test-target override, not a deployment knob; putting it in .env.example would suggest an operator should configure it in production.

entries.name: RUNNING_CONFIG_ALLOW_EMPTY
entries.reason: Says 'the containers I expect are not up yet' to scripts/check-running-config-drift.mjs. Valid on a machine with no running deployment; documenting it in the app's env file would suggest it is normal to carry.

entries.name: SEED_ALLOW_REMOTE
entries.reason: Deliberate opt-in that lets scripts/seed-dev.ts write fixture data to a non-local database. Keeping it out of .env.example is part of its safety: it should never be present-and-forgotten, only typed once when you mean it.

entries.name: SKIP_VERIFY
entries.reason: Skips the post-provision verification pass in scripts/provision-app-role.mjs, for hosts where the verifying connection cannot be opened. Recovery flag for the person running the script.

entries.name: DEPLOY_SHA
entries.reason: Written by the deploy workflow (deploy.yml) and read by scripts/deploy-migrate.ts:77 to tag a restore point with the revision being deployed. Machine-supplied provenance, never operator-supplied.

entries.name: WEBHOOK_SECRET_1
entries.reason: Per-endpoint fixture secret in scripts/seed-dev.ts:925. Falls back to a generated whsec_dev_<uuid>, so seeding works with nothing set; it is not a value a deployment configures.

entries.name: WEBHOOK_SECRET_2
entries.reason: Second fixture of the same kind (scripts/seed-dev.ts:934), for the two-endpoint seed scenario. Same generated-default reasoning as WEBHOOK_SECRET_1.

entries.name: ANALYZE
entries.reason: Build-invocation flag for next.config.mjs:108 ('ANALYZE=true npm run build') that adds the bundle-analyzer plugin. It changes what the BUILD produces, not what a deployment runs, and it is typed in front of the one command that needs it.

entries.name: SLIM_BUILD
entries.reason: Caps build workers to one so 'next build' fits in ~1.5GB on low-RAM boxes (next.config.mjs:37, set by scripts/start-slim.sh --build). Build-time only; leaving it in an env file would silently halve the speed of every later build on that machine.

entries.name: NEXT_DIST_DIR
entries.reason: Relocates the .next build directory, e.g. onto tmpfs for a faster build (#177, next.config.mjs:7). A property of the machine doing the building, and next.config creates it if absent, so it needs no documentation for operators.

entries.name: EXTERNAL_IP
entries.reason: Adds this machine's address to Next's allowedDevOrigins for remote development (next.config.mjs:18); unused in production, where the check is not applied. Its value is a live host address, which by AGENTS.md policy has no place in a file committed to this public repository — next.config warns and explains it instead.
